slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice
items: One tender spot on the bone
Pain at rest or at night

caption:
Toto squeezed in extra runs before race day, and now his shins ache. Hybi asked about the training, not the shoes.

Shin splints usually show up when running load rises faster than bone and muscle can adapt: a jump in weekly k's or a rush back after a break.

You often don't have to stop completely. Trim distance or pace, keep fitness ticking over with cycling or swimming, and build capacity with calf raises 15 × 3 sets and 30-second single-leg stands. Coming back, add distance first and speed later.

One tender spot on the bone, pain at rest or at night, or a limp needs checking before you run again. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio 🐰
